newsitem.title: MEXICO: Exports spur jobs surge in Central Mexico - CEESP.
newsitem.headline: Exports spur jobs surge in Central Mexico - CEESP.

text.p: Employment in the central Mexican state of Guanajuato has surged due to a thriving export sector, and the state has easily made up for the jobs lost in the 1994-5 economic crisis, a private sector study said.

The Private Sector Centre for Economic Studies (CEESP), one of Mexico's top think tanks, said in Guanajuato's industrial centre of Leon, 7,776 jobs were created in August, more than three times the 2,274 positions offered in July.

"Without a doubt the factors behind this increase are in foreign trade from manufacturing sectors such as leather and shoes, the textile industry and electro-domestic goods," Victor Medina Gama, head of CEESP in Leon, said.
A burst in construction activity fuelled by public sector-financed infrastructure projects also helped, he said.
But on the other hand, he noted, purchasing power was still suffering, with wage increases lagging inflation.
Last week, the government National Statistics Institute reported that Leon had the second lowest unemployment index of any city in Mexico, after the Pacific resort of Acapulco.

In Guanajuato as a whole, CEESP said, the turnaround was also pronounced. At the start of the year there was a deficit of 55,707 jobs, while in August there was a surplus of 21,063 jobs. In the intervening period, 76,770 positions were created.
